stories.title: Attacks and blockade enforcement around Hormuz
stories.what: Attacks on commercial shipping in and around the Strait of Hormuz have continued through November. UKMTO reports two tankers attacked in the Strait on Monday 16 November, both with engine-room fires and one vessel disabled, and an LPG tanker also suffered an engine-room fire after a Hormuz attack.
stories.why_it_matters: Hull strikes and crew-safety concerns raise war-risk premiums for Arabian Gulf liftings and shrink the pool of willing owners; depressed transit volumes reshape crude and product ton-miles.
stories.latest: Two further tanker attacks reported in the Strait on 16 November, plus an LPG tanker engine-room fire described as at least the 17th reported strike this month.
sources: UKMTO Reports Two Tanker Attacks in Strait of Hormuz
LPG tanker suffers engine room fire following Hormuz attack

stories.title: Attacks on shipping in the Black Sea and Baltic
stories.what: Drone strikes on merchant ships in the Black Sea have intensified. A Somali-flagged cargo ship carrying nearly 3,000 tonnes of wheat capsized off Bulgaria on Monday after what crew described as an attack by two sea drones, following earlier strikes near Romania's Sulina anchorage.
stories.why_it_matters: Strikes on ships and port infrastructure threaten grain and dry bulk loadings and add insurance and routing costs for any vessel calling in the region; proximity to NATO territory widens the risk area.
stories.latest: A wheat-laden cargo ship capsized off Bulgaria after a reported sea drone attack on Monday.
sources: Cargo Ship Capsizes Off Bulgaria After Reported Sea Drone Attack

stories.title: Sanctions and evasion in the shadow fleet
stories.what: Sanctions pressure on the shadow fleet is widening. The EU has imposed a new round of measures targeting shipowners, vessel managers, insurers and financial networks supporting Russia's shadow fleet, adding to earlier US designations across Cuban maritime entities and Iranian false-flag registry networks.
stories.why_it_matters: Designations of managers and insurers force charterers and underwriters to re-verify counterparties, documents and vessel positions, and can strand tonnage outside compliant trade.
stories.latest: EU announced new sanctions aimed at shadow fleet shipowners, managers and insurers.
sources: EU Targets Shadow Fleet Shipowners, Managers and Insurers in New Russia Sanctions

stories.title: US Jones Act waiver extended again
stories.what: A waiver allowing energy companies and traders to move oil, fertilizer and other commodities between US ports on foreign-flagged ships has been extended for another 90 days, with the pause now past 230 days.
stories.why_it_matters: The waiver keeps foreign-flag tonnage eligible for US coastwise cargoes, affecting demand for US-flag ships and the employment of product tankers in domestic trades.
sources: New US Policy Priorities Could Shape Future Shipping Markets

stories.title: Russian diesel flows and export restrictions
stories.what: A reported US-Russia arrangement on extra diesel for the US market has met political opposition, while Russia has extended a ban on most diesel exports to end-January.
stories.why_it_matters: Diesel export restrictions and any reopened Atlantic route reshape clean product tanker ton-miles and MR and LR employment.
sources: EU Targets Shadow Fleet Shipowners, Managers and Insurers in New Russia Sanctions

stories.title: US port fees on Chinese-built and Chinese-operated ships
stories.what: The US administration has formally extended its suspension of port fees targeting Chinese-built and Chinese-operated vessels for another two months while trade talks continue.
stories.why_it_matters: The fees, if reinstated, would change the cost of deploying Chinese-built tonnage into US trades and affect chartering preferences across sectors.
sources: New US Policy Priorities Could Shape Future Shipping Markets
